objective: Prove: (1) codes: if the law of a relation composes like cycles, every matroid of its systems is a direct sum of matroids representable over finite fields, and for an alphabet with no proper nontrivial pp-definable equivalence the relation is then a coset of a module code over a finite field; the Simonis-Ashikhmin almost affine code with the non-Pappus matroid therefore generates a law that fails elimination, exhibited by a three-copy system; (2) complexity: if a law with all constants added composes like cycles, its constraint problem is solvable in polynomial time, and with trivial tops a genuine Mal'tsev polymorphism exists; (3) counting: the lifted Z3 law and K4 compose like cycles but are not balanced, so their counting problems are #P-complete; state the conjecture that adding constants preserves composing like cycles, with evidence.
status: Proved by CYCLE-UTILITY-20261021-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof with explicit and randomized checks; the affine-tops results, Pappus's theorem, the Taylor criterion, the CSP dichotomy and the counting dichotomy cited). Codes: a law composing like cycles carries only matroids in R over finite fields, so the Simonis-Ashikhmin non-Pappus almost affine code generates a law that fails elimination, exhibited by a three-copy system. Complexity: a single-sorted law that still composes like cycles with all constants added has a Taylor polymorphism algebra, hence a polynomial-time constraint problem; with trivial tops a genuine Mal'tsev polymorphism exists; one-in-three, not-all-equal and 3-colouring fail elimination. Counting: the lifted Z3 law and K4 compose like cycles but are not balanced, so their counting problems are #P-complete. Constants can destroy composing like cycles (parity beside J, K4), so general tractability is open.
title: Proof: what composing like cycles is good for
